newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot and Continental in code sharing agreement.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot and Continental in code sharing agreement.

text.p: Russian flag carrier Aeroflot and Continental Airlines Inc. have signed a five-year deal to operate Moscow-New York flights and coordinate their schedules, reservations and tariffs, Aeroflot said Wednesday.
Aeroflot also said in a statement that both airlines agreed to use the new Russian-made Ilyushin Il-96M airliner, powered by U.S. engines and avionics, on joint operation routes.
Aeroflot spokeswoman Yulia Maryashkina said that Aeroflot and Continental would began joint operation of a new daily flight starting this fall between Moscow and Newark Airport.
The airport, located just west of New York in Newark, N.J., will serve as a hub to reach the 157 other U.S. cities to which Continental flies.

"It means that Russian passengers can buy tickets in Moscow for flights to these destinations just as U.S. passengers will fly from the United States to Russian and CIS destinations which Aeroflot serves," she said.
Maryashkina said that Aeroflot would continue operate three flights a week from Moscow's Sheremetyevo to New York's Kennedy Airport.
Aeroflot said it planned to buy 17 passenger versions and three cargo versions of the new Ilyushin planes over the next few years.
It also plans to cooperate with Continental on technical servicing, marketing and advertising, the statement said.
Aeroflot also plans to join Continental's frequent-flier programme soon.
Aeroflot's regular flights link Moscow with five Russian destinations and seven cities in other former Soviet states.
